chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not belittle the supplication of anyone, for it is accepted for the Jew and the Christian regarding you, but it is not accepted for them regarding their own selves.
ai.seo_question: Why is the supplication of a non-Muslim beggar accepted for the believer but not for themselves?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) encourages believers to respect the supplications of Jews and Christians, noting that their prayers for the believers' worldly benefit are accepted by God. However, their prayers for their own spiritual salvation or reward are not accepted, highlighting a distinction between divine acceptance of their pleas and their ultimate standing in the hereafter. This teaching underscores the value of humility and the universality of God's responsiveness to sincere prayer, regardless of the supplicant's faith tradition.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Do not belittle the supplication of anyone (from the beggars), for it gets Answered for the Jews and the Christians regarding you all, but it does not get Answered for them regarding their own selves’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm from abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following: “
You must not ignore anyone’s prayers; the prayers of Jews and Christians for you are answered, but they are not answered for themselves.”
